purpose: Test whether cumulative-NLL errors are predictable and whether a conservative local Top-5 override can improve same-frontier ranking without replacing NLL globally.

outputs: conditional Gold rank distribution when NLL Top1 is wrong
oracle upper bounds for perfect TopK correction

trust_classifier.label: 1 iff cumulative-NLL Top1 is Gold; 0 otherwise
features: NLL rank2 minus rank1 gaps for cumulative_nll, mean_nll_per_token, cumulative_regret, discrepancy_count, token_logprob, prefix_length, frontier_age
NLL rank5 minus rank1 cumulative_nll gap

top5_reranker.scope: Only states where Gold is within frozen cumulative-NLL Top5 during training; candidates restricted to frozen NLL ranks 1..5.
top5_reranker.pairs: Gold candidate versus every non-Gold candidate in NLL Top5; add symmetric negative pair.
candidate_features: within-Top5 zscore and percentile of prefix_length, cumulative_nll, mean_nll_per_token, cumulative_regret, discrepancy_count, token_logprob, local_token_rank, margin, entropy, frontier_age

hybrid_policy.name: NLL_CONSERVATIVE_OVERRIDE_V1
hybrid_policy.override_condition: trust classifier predicts P(NLL Top1 correct) < 0.20
hybrid_policy.override_action: choose highest reranker utility among cumulative-NLL ranks 2..5 only

note: All analyses are CPU/offline. Do not implement or run GPU search in this stage.
